title: Two-file manifest split — global discovery + per-project behavior, no per-project agent.json in v1
body:
The agent-discoverability artifact is split across two files with different audiences and lifecycles:

(1) Global discovery: `~/.dontpanic/agent-manifest.json` answers 'how does an agent find and invoke DontPanic on this machine?' Contains: DontPanic version, install source, CLI path, common commands, MCP server command (once F002 ships), safety rules, project registry pointer, supported intake types, default agent roles. Machine-level — NOT committed to project repos.

(2) Project behavior: `<repo>/.dontpanic/dontpanic.json` answers 'how should DontPanic operate in this project?' Contains: project key/name, plans dir, primary/auditor preferences, test/build commands, protected paths, allowed agents, target env/project references, governance docs, intake defaults. Project-level — committable when secret-free. Legacy `<repo>/.jarvis/jarvis.json` remains read-compatible. **This file already shipped in Phase A's F003 (plan 2026-05-03-001) — Phase B does not touch it except documentation of the rename compatibility.**

No per-project `agent-hints.json` in v1 — explicitly NOT created. Defer until evidence shows agents need a separate repo-local manifest.

Reason for two files, not one: collapsing them would force an OpenClaw-style external agent to re-discover DontPanic per-repo, or force a project to embed machine-level CLI paths that travel with the repo. Different questions, different audiences, different lifecycles. The OpenClaw integration story is about DontPanic being callable, not DontPanic-as-a-runtime — the global manifest is the primary integration surface.

How to apply: F001 lands the global manifest writer/reader. F003 (docs) cross-references both files but does not introduce new schema. Phase C's intake pipeline will read both at dispatch time.

title: MCP intake tool deferred to Phase C — explicitly NOT in F002 surface
body:
F002's MCP server exposes exactly 6 tools: `list_projects`, `validate_plan`, `dispatch`, `status`, `approve_gate`, `read_evidence`. **No `intake` tool.** This is a deliberate scope cut.

Reason: Phase C (intake pipeline) is the most-ambitious phase and will design the brief-to-plan transformation, sufficiency checking, discovery-budget rules, and cost-model implications. Exposing an `intake` MCP tool in Phase B would lock in a contract — input shape, output shape, error semantics — before Phase C has thought through the design. The cost of a premature `intake` contract is much higher than the cost of one extra round-trip when Phase C ships and adds it to the tool surface.

What callers do in the meantime: agents that want to start an intake flow against DontPanic in Phase B's window invoke the CLI directly (`dontpanic intake prd <file>`, etc.) once Phase C ships. The MCP `intake` tool lands as a Phase C feature, not a Phase B retrofit.

How to apply: F002's tool registration test must include a NEGATIVE assertion that `intake` is not in the tool list. The README + ECOSYSTEM.md examples (F003) must NOT show an MCP `intake` call — they show the 6 documented tools only. Phase C's plan will name the new MCP tool addition as part of its acceptance.

title: MCP server is local-only in Phase B — stdio default, localhost only if port-bound, no remote
body:
F002's `dontpanic mcp serve` is local-only. Transport is stdio by default; if a `--port` flag is added, it MUST bind only to 127.0.0.1 / ::1 — never to 0.0.0.0 or other interfaces. No HTTP listener accepting connections from non-loopback. No authentication scaffolding (deferred to a future remote-MCP plan if/when it becomes necessary).

Reason: Phase B's premise is that DontPanic is callable by ecosystem runtimes (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor). Those runtimes already solve remote agent access — they have Tailscale, SSH, ngrok, GitHub-based workflows, Claude dispatch, etc. Building a DontPanic-hosted remote daemon now would replicate solved problems and create a security surface (auth, rate-limiting, threat-model) that costs months. The right move is to ship the local surface, let the ecosystem use it, and defer remote-MCP until a real demand signal arrives. The threat model for a future daemon is pre-written in `docs/ROADMAP.md` — none of it is built now.

How to apply: F002 acceptance #3 requires no non-loopback HTTP listener in any code path. F002 tests verify by inspecting the server config / failed bind on 0.0.0.0. F003 docs explicitly say 'local-only' in the README quickstart. Future remote-MCP work is its own plan with its own threat model + acceptance — NOT a F002 expansion.

title: MCP mutating tools default to dry-run; require explicit `confirm: true`
body:
The `dispatch` and `approve_gate` MCP tools default to dry-run when invoked without `confirm: true` in the tool input. Dry-run returns the structured intent (which plan, which feature, which gate, what would happen) but does NOT execute the mutation. To actually dispatch a volley or clear a gate via MCP, the caller passes `confirm: true`.

Reason: This is symmetric with the `--force --yes` and `--yes` patterns Phase A's F002 (projects add/remove) established (D008 of plan 2026-05-03-001). Destructive intent is two-flag, not one-flag-with-prompt. In an MCP context where any chained agent could invoke the tool, defaulting to dry-run prevents 'agent autonomously dispatched 50 volleys overnight' failure modes. Operator-supplied tightening: 'Agent-facing docs should say: do not dispatch without user approval' (D007 below).

How to apply: F002 tool input schemas mark `confirm` as Boolean default-False. F002 tests parametric: `confirm` absent / `confirm: false` / `confirm: true` — first two return dry-run shape, third actually dispatches. F003 docs show every dispatch example with the `confirm: true` flag explicit, AND with a callout: 'surface the plan to the user before passing confirm: true'. The dry-run output shape is part of the F002 acceptance contract — agents need a deterministic preview surface.

title: MCP tools refuse arbitrary filesystem paths — registered projects/plans only
body:
Every F002 MCP tool that takes a plan or evidence path resolves it through Phase A's `_resolve_plan_dir` (registered projects only) OR refuses with a structured error. No tool accepts a bare filesystem path that resolves outside any registered project's plan_dir. `read_evidence` cannot read `/etc/passwd`. `validate_plan` cannot validate `/tmp/some-fake-plan-dir/`. `dispatch` cannot dispatch against an arbitrary directory.

Reason: An MCP server is a remote-execution-shaped attack surface even when local-only. A confused or malicious caller could supply paths the operator never intended DontPanic to touch. The registry-as-allowlist approach is the same shape Phase A's F003 used for `_resolve_plan_dir` (Step 4 cwd fallback is gated by file existence + registry resolution failing first). Phase B inherits and tightens that pattern: in MCP context, the Step 4 cwd fallback is REMOVED — only registry-resolved paths are accepted via the MCP surface.

How to apply: F002 implements a `_resolve_safe_path(plan_id_or_path)` helper that wraps `_resolve_plan_dir` with stricter MCP semantics (no Step 4 cwd carveout). F002 tests parametric over: absolute path outside any registered project (refuses), relative path resolving outside (refuses), name not in registry (refuses), bare cwd-relative path (refuses), registered-name-or-path (resolves). The tool surface is constrained to the registry — it is not a general filesystem API.

title: Manifest must be secret-free and regenerable
body:
Two invariants on `~/.dontpanic/agent-manifest.json` (legacy `~/.jarvis/agent-manifest.json` read fallback only):

(1) **Secret-free.** No API keys, no service-account JSON paths, no auth tokens. The schema rejects fields containing `_token` / `_key` / `_secret` (Pydantic-level field-name validation). The `cli_path` field is OK because it's a binary location, not a credential. Sanitization scan against a written manifest must report 0 findings — same regression suite Phase A's F002 / F022 use.

(2) **Regenerable + idempotent.** Re-running the writer with the same inputs (same DontPanic version, same install source, same CLI path) produces a byte-identical file. No timestamps in the manifest body. No nondeterministic ordering of list fields. Operators (or a future `dontpanic bootstrap` helper) can rewrite the manifest from scratch and recover from corruption.

Reason: The manifest is machine-level discovery, not a credential surface. Mixing secrets in would require ACL hardening, file-mode discipline, and a leak-detection threat model that Phase B does not have time for. Regenerable means the manifest is a derivable artifact, not source-of-truth — operators can `rm` it and re-bootstrap without losing state.

How to apply: F001 schema-level field-name validator rejects `*_token` / `*_key` / `*_secret`. F001 tests include a regenerability test (write twice with same inputs, assert byte-identical) and a sanitization-clean test (scan a written manifest with the existing sanitization_check, assert 0 findings). F003 docs explicitly note that operators can `dontpanic manifest init --force --yes` to rewrite at will — no migration step required.

title: Agent-facing docs must say: do not dispatch without user approval
body:
F003 (discoverability docs) AND F001 (manifest `safety_rules` field) MUST include a literal string instructing agent callers: do not dispatch without user approval. Specific wording (or operator-approved equivalent): 'Always surface the plan to the user before calling `dispatch(confirm=true)`. Do NOT auto-confirm.'

This string must appear verbatim in three places:
  - F001's `AgentManifest.safety_rules` field (so any agent reading the manifest sees it)
  - README's 'How agents call DontPanic' section
  - `docs/ECOSYSTEM.md` (already has the OpenClaw caller recipe; add the safety rule explicitly)

Reason: This is the line between 'DontPanic is a useful tool agents call' and 'DontPanic is the agent's autonomous backend'. The product discipline is plan-first / human-approved-first (PRODUCT.md 'Important Product Principle' section). MCP makes it trivially easy for a chained agent to call dispatch; a calmly-worded safety rule embedded in the manifest + every example reduces that risk substantially without requiring runtime enforcement.

How to apply: F003 acceptance #3 makes this string verbatim-required and verifiable by parametric test (grep all three locations for the exact string). If F003 wants to use slightly different wording in different surfaces, the operator must approve the variant at lock time and the test must be updated to match.

title: External directory listings (PyPI, MCP directory, GitHub topics) are evidence-of-readiness, not hard acceptance
body:
F003 ships a publish-readiness checklist (`docs/DISCOVERABILITY.md`) covering PyPI metadata fields, GitHub topic tags, MCP-directory listing requirements, README badges. **Submitting to those external directories is NOT a Phase B acceptance item.** F003 acceptance is satisfied when the checklist exists, items are marked `[ ] not yet submitted`, and the metadata fields needed for future submission are correct in `pyproject.toml` / README.

Reason: External submissions are committment surfaces. Submitting to PyPI as `dontpanic-orchestrate` is a versioning + maintainability promise — once the name is taken, future renames are painful. Submitting to the MCP directory is a public-listing claim — once listed, anyone can install + report bugs. Phase B's job is to make DontPanic ready for those submissions; the operator decides when to actually submit (probably after a real OpenClaw integration validates the surface). Conflating 'ready' with 'submitted' would force premature publish decisions and create a stop-the-line for issues that should be deferred.

How to apply: F003 acceptance language explicitly says 'evidence of readiness, not delivery commitments'. The DISCOVERABILITY.md file uses `[ ]` checkboxes marked `not yet submitted` so it's clear what's done vs queued. Future submission rides a separate operator action — likely a small post-Phase-B housekeeping commit, not a feature in any plan.

title: Plan ID brand policy — committed IDs are durable, drafts use DontPanic
body: Plan IDs and committed plan folder names are durable identifiers. Once committed, a plan ID may be referenced by parent plans, evidence_refs, scripts, audit trails, decision logs, and transcripts. Historical committed plans containing `jarvis` in the slug stay as-is; renaming them requires high-churn cascade updates for low value. Draft or untracked plans should be renamed to use `dontpanic` before they are committed. New plan IDs use `dontpanic` for brand references. Carve-out: `jarvis` remains allowed when it is a load-bearing technical reference, such as work that explicitly modifies `scripts/jarvis_doctor.py`, `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/`, `JARVIS_*` compatibility env vars, or historical artifacts whose names already contain `jarvis`. Current runtime layout: new installs prefer `~/.dontpanic/`, `<repo>/.dontpanic/dontpanic.json`, `DONTPANIC_HOME`, and `python -m dontpanic_orchestrate`; legacy `~/.jarvis/`, `<repo>/.jarvis/jarvis.json`, `JARVIS_HOME`, `python -m jarvis_orchestrate`, and the `jarvis` CLI alias remain compatibility fallbacks where implemented. Durable memory mirror: `feedback_plan_id_brand_policy.md`.

title: Phase B locked. Per-feature execution paths committed: F001/F003/F004 direct, F002 volley
body:
Plan flipped from `status: draft` to `status: active`. Per the plan's 'Execution path (deferred per feature)' section, the per-feature path commitments are now formal:

**F001 — Global agent manifest** → DIRECT. Modeled on Phase A F001/F002 (`global_config.py`, `projects_registry.py`): Pydantic v2 schema with `extra='forbid'`, writer/reader/bootstrap helpers, `dontpanic manifest {init|show}` CLI subcommand, comprehensive test module. Risk surface is mechanical: schema correctness, regenerable + idempotent invariants (D006), secret-free invariant (D006), env-var precedence (`DONTPANIC_HOME` preferred + `JARVIS_HOME` legacy fallback per the runtime layout established in commit `1db2464`). Direct path with TDD red tests first matches the F001/F002 close-out pattern that worked cleanly in Phase A.

**F002 — Thin local MCP server** → VOLLEY. Touches a new external surface that ecosystem agents will call; the cross-cutting tightenings (mutating-tools-default-to-dry-run per D004, local-only per D003, path-validation per D005, no-`intake`-tool per D002) are exactly the kind of unsafe-default + missed-call-site bugs adversarial review catches better than single-pass implementation. The volley audit-focus list will mirror F003 of plan 2026-05-03-001: missed call sites, wrong default semantics, unsafe path acceptance, intake-tool scope creep, edge cases in confirm:true vs absent vs false, log-channel discipline (stdout reserved for MCP protocol).

**F003 — Agent discoverability docs** → DIRECT. Doc-only feature: README snippets, ECOSYSTEM.md addendum, new DISCOVERABILITY.md publish-readiness checklist. Verification is parametric tests asserting verbatim safety-rule string presence + `mcp.json` snippets parse + cross-references resolve. No dispatch-path code touched.

**F004 — LLM-authored plan schema docs** → DIRECT. Doc-only feature: `docs/AUTHORING_PLANS.md` with the 5 sections (layout / minimum / examples / sufficiency boundary / validation). Verification asserts the embedded examples extract and pass `plan_loader.load`. Explicit non-goal recorded in the doc itself: this is authoring guidance, not the Phase C intake engine.

**Sequencing**: F001 first (manifest is what F002+F003 advertise/document), then F002 volley (the substantive cross-cutting feature), then F003+F004 doc surfaces in parallel. Close each feature's evidence before flipping the next to `passes:true` per the F001/F002/F003 Phase A pattern.

If F001 surfaces a defect that F002's tightenings should also catch, surface it as a feedback memory entry before dispatching F002 — same volley-failure-taxonomy discipline used for F003 of plan 003.

title: F001 close-out — agent manifest shipped direct; EC5 classifier purity test queued as separate platform fix
body:
F001 (global agent manifest at `~/.dontpanic/agent-manifest.json`) shipped via direct path per D010. Verification:

- Targeted: 53/53 tests green in `test_f001_agent_manifest.py` (schema + load/save + regenerable + secret-free + bootstrap + CLI init/show + cwd-arbitrary).
- Full suite excluding the pre-existing-broken `test_ec5_classifier.py`: 748 passed, 6 skipped (was 702+6 before F001; +46 = 41 ec5 tests excluded + 53 F001 added - 48 net visible since ec5 file is excluded entirely).
- Ruff: clean across `agent_manifest.py`, `cli.py`, `tests/test_f001_agent_manifest.py`.
- Sanitization: 0 findings, 602 files scanned.
- Plan validates against agent-conventions v1.0 schema.

**What landed**:

(1) New module `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/agent_manifest.py` (~250 lines): `AgentManifest` Pydantic v2 model with `extra='forbid'` and locked schema_version='1.0'; `InstallSource` Literal {pipx, pip-editable, source}; optional `McpServerSpec` (populated by F002, omitted from on-disk JSON in Phase B F001 ship); `manifest_path()`/`load_manifest()` (total — missing→None, invalid-JSON→WARN+None, schema-violation→WARN+None); `write_manifest()` regenerable + idempotent at the byte level (D006); `bootstrap_manifest()` collects host inputs (`__version__`, install_source, cli_path) and seeds `safety_rules` with the canonical 'do not dispatch without user approval' rule (D007). Import-time guard `_assert_no_credential_shaped_fields()` rejects any future schema field with `_token`/`_key`/`_secret` substrings (D006).

(2) New CLI subcommand `dontpanic manifest {init|show}` wired into `cli.py`: `init` flags `--force`/`--yes`/`--cli-path`/`--install-source`/`--json`; `show` flags `--json`. `--force` requires `--yes` for non-interactive use (parity with `dontpanic projects add` per D008 of plan 2026-05-03-001 / D004 here). `init` collision exits 2 with explicit message; `show` missing exits 2.

(3) New test file `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f001_agent_manifest.py` (~360 lines, 53 tests across 8 classes): TestSchema (minimum-valid + extra-forbid + install-source enum +/- + credential-shaped extras rejected + design-discipline schema-introspection + safety-rules carry canonical string + required-fields-missing); TestPaths (DONTPANIC_HOME + JARVIS_HOME legacy fallback); TestLoadSave (missing→None + roundtrip + invalid-JSON→WARN + extra-field→WARN + creates-home + legacy-JARVIS_HOME-still-writes); TestRegenerable (byte-identical rewrite + no-ISO-timestamp + None-fields-excluded); TestSecretFree (no credential substrings in body); TestBootstrap (version-pinned + schema-version-1.0 + safety-rule-verbatim + idempotent + project_registry_path under DONTPANIC_HOME + supported_commands core set + mcp_server omitted in F001); TestCLIInit + TestCLIShow + TestCLIDispatch.

**Caveat queued for separate platform fix**: `test_ec5_classifier.py::test_classifier_is_pure_no_io` is broken post-directory-rename (Jarvis → DontPanic, then DontPanic dir at `/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/`). Two failure mechanisms intertwine:

  (a) The test patches `Path.stat` at the class level via `monkeypatch.setattr(Path, 'stat', _explode)`. When the test's underlying assertion fails (`assert classify_ec5_severity(audit) == 'none'`), pytest's `_traceback_filter` (`_pytest/_code/code.py:95`) calls `code.path` which calls `p.exists()` which internally calls `self.stat()` — still patched as `_explode` — turning a normal test failure into INTERNALERROR.

  (b) The actual assertion is now failing because `classify_ec5_severity` (or `target_context_prelude` it depends on) is touching disk after the rename. Most likely: `target_context_prelude.resolve_repo()` calls `subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'])` and post-rename the cwd or git context is hitting Path methods the classifier didn't trigger before.

  Reproducer: `PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m pytest 'scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_ec5_classifier.py::test_classifier_is_pure_no_io' -p no:cacheprovider`. Excluded from F001 close-out per scope discipline — F001 is the agent-manifest surface; ec5_classifier purity is a separate platform concern. Queued as a platform fix slice alongside the lifecycle-staged-gates and 600s-subprocess-timeout caveats from D009 of plan 2026-05-03-001. The fix is two-part: (i) replace the class-level `Path.stat` monkeypatch with a more surgical instance-level or context-manager seam so a test failure cannot leak into pytest's traceback machinery; (ii) audit `target_context_prelude` for incidental disk I/O the classifier shouldn't trigger (probably make `resolve_repo` accept a pre-resolved repo arg in the classifier path).

**Operator-canonical command surface from this commit forward**: `dontpanic ...` is the canonical end-user CLI (e.g., `dontpanic manifest init`, `dontpanic projects add`). `python -m dontpanic_orchestrate ...` is reserved for module-invocation / packaging verification / console-script-independent execution. Internal Python imports stay `from jarvis_orchestrate import ...` until the separately-planned internal rename slice lands.

title: F002 close-out — MCP server accepted after i1 fixes; remaining needs_changes was environmental
body: F002 (thin local MCP server) shipped via the locked volley path from D010. The volley terminated stopped_no_progress after 2 rounds, but direct review shows the F002 deliverable is complete and all substantive i0 audit findings were fixed in i1. Iteration 0 surfaced four findings: HIGH security traversal escape in relative path handling, MEDIUM missing traversal tests, MEDIUM ruff-format dirty files, and ADVISORY untracked F002 files. Iteration 1 fixed the security issue by enforcing resolved.relative_to(root_resolved) on relative path candidates, added 20 traversal refusal cases, ran ruff format, and staged the new source/test files. Iteration 1 auditor needs_changes was environmental/noise: pytest aborted before collection because the auditor sandbox had no usable writable tempdir, and the auditor also flagged stale i0 envelope inconsistency caused by the prior timeout/truncated envelope pattern. These are not F002 feature defects. Direct-review verification in the operator shell: 130/130 F001+F002 focused tests green; full orchestrate suite excluding the known queued test_ec5_classifier.py caveat green at 825 passed, 6 skipped; ruff check clean; ruff format --check clean on F002 files; sanitization clean with 614 files scanned; manifest population verified (bootstrap_manifest emits mcp_server={command:'dontpanic', args:['mcp','serve']} and supported_commands contains mcp); F002 registers exactly six tools and no intake tool per D002. Close-out accepts the feature on direct review rather than re-dispatching to chase a clean envelope, consistent with D011 caveats and the F003-of-plan-003 600s-timeout precedent. The ec5_classifier purity regression and subprocess timeout/envelope-flush issue remain queued platform fixes and are not F002 blockers.

title: Plan close-out — status flip active → completed via exempt-flow
body:
Fourth close-out in the Tier 1 close-out batch (after 2026-05-04-001 canonical-module flip, 2026-05-02-003 nested-orch v1, 2026-05-03-001 Phase A global install + registry).

All four features (F001/F002/F003/F004) shipped passes:true; F001/F003/F004 direct, F002 via volley with terminal stopped_no_progress operator-accepted on direct review per D012 (i0 substantive findings — HIGH traversal escape + 2 MEDIUM + 1 advisory — fixed in i1; remaining i1 needs_changes was environmental: auditor sandbox tempdir + stale-envelope inconsistency from the timeout pattern, not feature defects).

Eight-step close-out executed with corrected discipline: (1) `git ls-tree HEAD -- docs/plans/2026-05-03-003-feat-agent-access-manifest-thin-mcp/` enumerated 14 tracked files; worktree had 15 — the diff surfaced an UNTRACKED `INBOX.md` (inverse of the Plan 2026-05-02-003 tracked-but-absent failure mode). The supervisor wrote INBOX.md during the F002 volley on 2026-05-04 but it never made it into git. Plan 2026-05-03-001's INBOX was tracked; this gap was hygiene, not content. (2) Validate exits 0 across plan.md frontmatter, features.json, and 5 audit envelopes (F002 i0+i1 implementer + auditor + signoff); auxiliary `evidence/f002-generated/gate-state.json` not in validator's audit/ scan path. (3) Per-feature evidence comprehensive (`evidence/f00{1,2,3,4}-closeout-memo.md`); D-history captures lock + scope + close-out reasoning (D001–D014 including D012's full F002 acceptance reasoning that explicitly cites the F003-of-plan-2026-05-03-001 600s-timeout precedent). (4) Plan-level memo at `evidence/plan-closeout-memo.md` adds value beyond per-feature evidence by: (i) cross-feature synthesis F001+F002+F003+F004 = 'callable by ecosystem agents' arc, (ii) cross-plan stopped_no_progress pattern table (Phase A F003 + Phase B F002 — both operator-accepted, both rooted in distinct platform issues), (iii) cross-link to follow-up plans (`2026-05-04-003` timeout/envelope durability + `2026-05-04-004` ec5 classifier purity), (iv) brand-state note (this plan is DontPanic-native from day zero — first such), (v) INBOX hygiene resolution + the (HEAD-worktree)+(worktree-HEAD) bidirectional partial-clone-and-untracked check, (vi) Phase A→B→C/D arc framing with C explicitly excluded from F002's MCP tool surface per D002. (5) D015 appended without reconstructing existing entries — single-line append after verifying D001–D014 sequence is intact. (6) `dontpanic plan close docs/plans/2026-05-03-003-feat-agent-access-manifest-thin-mcp/` — `goal_type=None` consumes the exempt-by-absence branch of the F2 completion gate. (7) Re-validate exits 0 with `status: completed`. (8) Commit scoped to this plan dir; INBOX.md picked up under git tracking with the close-out (operator directive 'Commit only that plan directory' is permissive on plan-dir scope, restrictive on cross-dir contamination — INBOX is in-scope by literal directive, and including it makes plan-dir state consistent with Plan 2026-05-03-001).

Reason: Phase B is the calling-pattern surface for ecosystem agents — global manifest (find DontPanic), thin MCP server with security-defaulted six-tool surface (call DontPanic), discoverability + LLM-authoring docs. F002's stopped_no_progress terminal is the second instance of that breaker shape this batch (Phase A F003 was the first); both were operator-accepted on direct review. Pattern flagged in plan-level memo as platform-shape signal, not current scope. Brand state is DontPanic-native from day zero (first such plan); legacy `~/.jarvis/` only wired as F001 read fallback.

How to apply: nested orchestration is NOT used for this close-out (operator-confirmed). Phase C drafting remains demand-driven (D012 substrate-vs-layer discipline carried forward from nested-orch v1 plan); MCP intake tool explicitly excluded from F002 per D002 — exposing intake before Phase C designs the contract would lock in a shape not yet designed.
